10.1002_adfm.77183: Electrochromic batteries based on transition metal oxides (e.g., WO 3 , LTO, NiO) or metal electrodeposition show great promise in applications like smart windows and flexible electronics. However, transition metal oxide systems often involve complex fabrication, limited energy storage capability, and non‐neutral monochromatic coloration, whereas metal‐electrodeposition systems suffer from dendrite‐related reliability issues and irreversible energy dissipation. In this work, we develop a low‐cost multicolor electrochromic battery based on reversible polyiodide (I n − ) electrodeposition, using a solution‐processable cathode comprising poly(3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA). The conductive PEDOT matrix suppresses electrochemical polarization in I − /I n − redox, enabling a large areal capacity (8700 mAh m −2 at 0.25 mA cm −2 ), superior energy density (11 200 mWh m −2 at 3250 mW m −2 ), and high energy efficiency (92.7%), while the uniformly distributed PVA enhances the film stability. Furthermore, 1‐butyl‐3‐methylimidazolium methanesulfonate is added to inhibit the polyiodide shuttle effect, enabling the device to undergo 10 000 optical cycles with ∼100% optical retention. Critically, the intrinsic transparent‐to‐blue electrochromism of PEDOT synergizes with the color modulation (yellow‐to‐brown) enabled by controlling polyiodide deposition time, facilitating voltage/duration‐programmable multicolor states. Overall, this design addresses several limitations hindering the practical deployment of electrochromic devices, including low areal capacity and efficiency, poor cycling stability, monochromatic coloration, and costly fabrication.
10.1002_adfm.78511: Interfacial electronic coupling has emerged as an effective strategy to regulate the electronic structure of sulfur hosts and enhance their catalytic activity toward lithium polysulfides conversion in lithium–sulfur batteries. However, using atomically dispersed metal sites as local electronic regulators to modulate interfacial charge redistribution and electronically activate thermodynamically stable 2H‐MoS 2 remains insufficiently understood. Herein, a 2D heterostructure was constructed by coupling stable 2H‐MoS 2 with Co single‐atom‐anchored reduced graphene oxide (MoS 2 ‐Co‐rGO). Experimental characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that the Co single atoms regulate the electronic state of the rGO substrate and strengthen interfacial charge redistribution, thereby reconstructing the local electronic environment of adjacent Mo centers and electronically activating 2H‐MoS 2 . The electronically reconstructed MoS 2 exhibits enhanced interactions with lithium polysulfides, accelerated interfacial charge‐transfer kinetics, and facilitated Li 2 S nucleation/decomposition. Consequently, the MoS 2 ‐Co‐rGO/S cathode delivers a high specific capacity of 1328 mAh g −1 at 0.2 C and a low‐capacity decay rate of 0.042% per cycle over 800 cycles at 2 C. Moreover, an Ah‐level pouch cell achieves a capacity of 14 Ah and a gravimetric energy density of 474 Wh kg −1 . This work provides a single‐atom‐regulated interfacial electronic‐reconstruction strategy for activating stable 2H‐MoS 2 toward high‐energy‐density lithium–sulfur batteries.
10.1002_anie.202511266: Developing single‐atom catalysts (SACs) with asymmetric coordination configurations is essential for enhancing peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation in Fenton‐like reactions. However, precisely regulating the electronic structure and coordination environment of metal centers to further improve activation kinetics remains a key challenge. Herein, we designed asymmetric CoN 1 O 2 single atoms (SAs) sites and Co nanoclusters (NCs) that were spatially confined in highly graphitized carbon layers and supported on holey MXene nanosheet (Co SA‐NC /H 20 MX) via a dual‐coordination microenvironment strategy. The Co SA‐NC /H 20 MX catalyst demonstrated exceptional performance on bisphenol A (BPA) removal, achieving a corrected rate constant ( k value ) of 2750 min −1 M −1 and a total organic carbon removal efficiency of 78.2%. Mechanistic studies revealed that BPA removal was dominated by a nonradical electron transfer process (ETP, ∼100%), which facilitated rapid polymerization of BPA. Density functional theory calculations demonstrated that Co NCs synergistically enhanced the ability of asymmetric CoN 1 O 2 SAs sites to adsorb and activate PMS, significantly accelerating interfacial charge transfer. Furthermore, a catalytic membrane fabricated by crosslinking of Co SA‐NC /H 20 MX and graphene achieved 100% BPA removal in single‐pass mode with a hydraulic retention time of just 40 ms over 24 h of continuous operation. This work provides new insights into designing high‐performance catalysts for pollutant removal via ETP‐driven polymerization pathways.
10.1021_acs.est.6c05431: Nanoplastics (NPs) and antibiotics co-occur in wastewater systems, but how NP size influences antibiotic biodegradation by specialized degraders remains unclear. Here, we investigated the effects of europium-doped polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs; PS20 and PS100) on sulfadiazine biodegradation by Arthrobacter sp. strain D2. Modified Gompertz modeling revealed two contrasting inhibition regimes. For PS100, inhibition was dominated by lag-phase prolongation, with no detectable sulfadiazine removal over 48 h at a PS100 concentration of 100 mg L–1. In contrast, PS20 reduced the maximum sulfadiazine degradation rate by ∼40% while causing only minor changes in lag time, indicating rate-dominated inhibition. Quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring at a model sulfadiazine-enriched interface showed that PS100 markedly reduced the deposition of NP-pre-exposed cells, whereas PS20 only partially impaired adhesion. Transmission electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy further revealed intracellular accumulation of PS20, whereas PS100 remained predominantly extracellular. Phase-specific physiological measurements and transcriptomics suggested that PS20 induced oxidative-stress responses associated with reduced sulfadiazine biodegradation rates, whereas PS100 elicited dose-dependent transcriptional changes during lag-phase extension. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that nanoplastics impair antibiotic attenuation through distinct size-dependent mechanisms involving interface-associated constraints and intracellular interference, highlighting particle size as a key determinant of antibiotic fate in plastic-contaminated wastewater environments.
10.1021_acs.inorgchem.5c04059: Herein, we present a theoretical framework to uncover the crucial roles of interlayer magnetic exchange of two-dimensional hexaaminobenzene (HAB)-based metal–organic frameworks (TM-HAB) catalysts on electrocatalytic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance. Through multistage screening, monolayer Fe-HAB-I and Co-HAB-I were identified as optimal for 4e – and 2e – ORR pathways, respectively. Grand Canonical Density Functional Theory (GC-DFT) and Monte Carlo simulations revealed monolayer Co-HAB-I prefers to a 2e – ORR with an onset potential of 0.95 V vs RHE under alkaline conditions, while Fe-HAB-I exhibits 4e – ORR activity at the onset potential of 0.73 V vs RHE in acidic environments. For experimentally relevant multilayer systems, GC-DFT calculation of bilayer Fe-HAB-II highlights the critical role of interlayer magnetic coupling: the ferromagnetic (FM II ) state demonstrates a markedly higher onset potential than the antiferromagnetic (AFM II ) state at pH = 13. Notably, Fe-HAB-II in the FM II state achieves a theoretical onset potential of 1.17 V vs RHE, closely aligning with experimental observations (1.02 V vs RHE), thereby validating the crucial roles of interlayer spin exchange on ORR property. This work underscores the pivotal influence of interlayer magnetic interactions in optimizing two-dimensional electrocatalysts for ORR.
10.1021_acsami.5c19410: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are considered a promising alternative to lithium-ion batteries due to the abundance and low cost of sodium resources, wherein cathode materials play a critical role in determining their performance. The vanadium-based phosphate Na 1+ x V x Ti 2- x (PO 4 ) 3 is considered a promising cathode for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) due to its high capacity and structural stability. However, the high reactivity of V 3+ during redox reactions results in rapid capacity fading, while a higher Ti 3+ proportion reduces the achievable capacity. In this work, we systematically tune the V/Ti ratio of NASICON-type Na 1+ x V x Ti 2- x (PO 4 ) 3 to obtain cathode materials with optimized electrochemical performance and study the crystal structure and battery performance of Na 2 VTi(PO 4 ) 3 . Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were used to predict the voltage plateau and phase stability of Na 2 VTi(PO 4 ) 3, indicating a low volume change (∼6.89%). Experiments indicated that elevated vanadium content promotes the activity of V 2+/3+ and V 3+/4+ redox couples, which facilitates multielectron reactions and improves specific capacity. Meanwhile, the Ti 3+/4+ redox couple contributes to structural integrity and supplementary charge compensation. Leveraging the synergy between V and Ti, the Na 1.6 V 0.6 Ti 1.4 (PO 4 ) 3 composition was determined to be optimal. This material exhibited an initial discharge capacity of 144.83 mAh g – 1 at 0.2C, with a capacity retention of 92.42% over 500 cycles, as well as outstanding rate performance and cycling reversibility. This study provides both theoretical and experimental guidance for designing high-performance, long-life cathode materials for SIBs.
10.1021_acsami.5c19977: The severe shuttle effect of polysulfides for high-performance lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries leads to poor reversibility and cyclability at high rates, greatly hindering their practical applications. Here, we design a Phyllostachys edulis -derived microporous carbon–sulfur (denoted as MPC@S) cathode with physical nanoconfinement and chemical C–S bonding for high-rate Li–S batteries. The high pore volume can physically confine sulfur and polysulfides into microporous carbon to achieve good structural stability of the electrode during cycling. Moreover, the strong chemical C–S bonding interaction between MPC and sulfur can effectively improve the utilization of the active material and enhance redox reaction kinetics at high rates. Due to the synergistic combination of physical and chemical confinement of sulfur and polysulfides, the Li–S battery with MPC@S cathode delivers an initial specific discharge capacity of 1070.06 mAh g –1 at 167.5 mA g –1 and achieves good cyclability with a high average Coulombic efficiency of >97.88% at 1675 mA g –1 for 500 cycles with a low decay rate of 0.0912% per cycle. This work provides a facile strategy for the large-scale fabrication of high-performance biomass-derived composite cathodes for high-rate Li–S batteries and brings deep insights into structure–property relationships of high-capacity electrodes for next-generation lithium batteries.
10.1039_d6ta04097g: This review traces the evolution of PSCs employing ionic liquids as solvents in perovskite precursor solutions and discusses the potential breakthroughs and challenges of ionic-liquid-based solvent systems.
10.3389_fpls.2026.1954222: Introduction Microplastics and heavy metals cooccur in freshwater habitats, yet it remains unclear whether microplastics intensify metal toxicity or redirect the dominant mode of plant injury. Methods We exposed the floatingleaved aquatic plant Nymphaea `Black Beauty' for 28 d to control conditions, copper (Cu) alone, polypropylene microplastics (PPMPs) alone, or combined Cu and PPMP stress. Wholeplant phenotype, relative growth rate, leaf chlorosis and necrosis, root scanning electron microscopy, gas exchange, chlorophyll fluorescence, malondialdehyde (MDA), and antioxidant enzymes were integrated to distinguish structural damage from functional inhibition. Results Cu alone produced a necrosisdominated response: relative growth rate decreased by approximately 65%, net photosynthetic rate (Pn) by 54%, effective PSII quantum yield (ΦPSII) by 52%, and electron transport rate (ETR) by 47%, whereas MDA increased by 58% and necrotic area reached 26.4%. PPMPs alone caused moderate growth inhibition and chlorosis, with a numerically higher nonphotochemical quenching (NPQ) mean and little lipid peroxidation. Factorial analysis detected Cu × PP interactions for selected endpoints, including growth, necrosis, Pn, NPQ, ETR, and POD; these endpointwise tests were exploratory. Necrotic area declined to 2.1%, but growth and photosynthesis remained strongly inhibited. The density of morphologically assigned PPlike structures in processed root sections was 4.16fold higher under combined exposure than under PPMPs alone. Under coexposure, Pn declined while no differences in stomatal conductance or transpiration from the control were detected, while ΦPSII, ETR, and NPQ decreased markedly. The lower NPQ mean was consistent with reduced regulated thermal dissipation under the measurement conditions but was not diagnostic of a specific photoprotective defect. POD activity increased by approximately 40%, whereas SOD activity decreased by 35%, showing an enzymespecific antioxidant pattern rather than demonstrating enhanced overall detoxification. Discussion Thus, under the shared 2% Tween20 background, Cu -PP coexposure produced a lownecrosis, highfunctionalinhibition phenotype consistent with an important nonstomatal component. These responses do not establish altered Cu distribution, particle internalization, or detoxification.
